name: EDMONDSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Energy Discrimination Elimination Act of 2022 is unconstitutional as applied to the Oklahoma Public Employees Retirement System because it creates a dual purpose for investment decisions, conflicting with the state constitution's mandate for an exclusive purpose for public retirement funds.

name: Kuehn, V.C.J.
description: Concurred, arguing that HB 2783 directly conflicts with the clear and unambiguous constitutional mandate for TSET directors to serve fixed seven-year terms, thereby subverting the independence of the TSET Board.

name: GURICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that S.B. 632 is unconstitutional as it creates business court divisions whose judges are district judges and must be elected, but the Act mandates an appointment process, violating Article VII, Section 9 of the Oklahoma Constitution, and its unconstitutional provisions are not severable.

name: ROWE, C.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that while the Legislature can create a new court division, S.B. 632's provisions for selecting judges conflict with the constitutional requirement for elected judicial officers.

name: KUEHN, V.C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Court should not have exercised original jurisdiction due to petitioners' lack of standing and premature analysis without a developed factual record.

name: JETT, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Court should not have assumed original jurisdiction because there was no urgent need for an expedited decision, as interim relief could prevent harm, and the case should have proceeded in district court.

name: KANE, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: KANE, J.
description: Concurred, argued that current sex offender residency restrictions are not punitive and can be applied retroactively without violating ex post facto clauses.

name: KUEHN, V.C.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that SORA should be considered a civil statute in its entirety by overturning Starkey, and that the record was insufficient to prove the residency restrictions are punitive in effect.

name: COMBS, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the retroactive application of current residency restrictions increases punishment for Donaldson's prior conviction, violating the ex post facto clause of the Oklahoma Constitution.

name: EDMONDSON, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the retroactive application of current residency restrictions increases punishment for Donaldson's prior conviction, violating the ex post facto clause of the Oklahoma Constitution.

name: Combs, J.
description: Concurred, argued that there are no material or irreconcilable conflicts between the GTCA and OADA regarding notice provisions, and therefore GTCA notice is required for OADA claims against governmental entities.

name: DARBY, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Governor, as the Chief Magistrate with supreme executive power, has the authority to choose counsel to represent the state's interests in a case where he is a named defendant, and the Attorney General's authority to assume control is subordinate to this.

name: COMBS, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Governor's participation as a named defendant includes the choice of counsel, and the Attorney General can appear ex officio, but believes the underlying case is moot because previous Treat v. Stitt decisions already found the compacts invalid.

name: LUMPKIN, Judge
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court abused its discretion by applying the Exclusionary Rule to suppress evidence for a 'knock and announce' rule violation, as the rule's purpose is not to shield evidence and other deterrents exist.

name: ROWLAND, P.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the exclusionary rule should rarely be employed for statutory violations unless the statute explicitly provides for it, and overruled prior inconsistent case law.

name: MUSSEMAN, V.P.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the exclusionary rule is inapplicable and highlighted concerns about the court's standard of review and district courts exceeding the scope of motions to quash.

name: KAUGER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the medical district is subject to lawsuits through its board of trustees to the same extent as municipalities and counties, and the GTCA applies to preclude recovery when workers' compensation benefits have been awarded.

name: Winchester, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the St. Isidore Contract violates state and federal law and is unconstitutional because a public charter school must be nonsectarian and cannot evangelize a specific faith while sponsored by the State.

name: Rowe, V.C.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that Article 1, Section 5 of the Oklahoma Constitution mandates that public charter schools are nonsectarian but dissented to the remainder of the Majority's opinion.

name: Kuehn, J.
description: Dissented, argued that St. Isidore would not become a "state actor" merely by contracting with the State to provide educational choice, and that excluding private entities from contracting based solely on religious affiliation would violate the Free Exercise Clause.

name: KUEHN, J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the initiative petition should go to a vote but the court should not determine its constitutionality pre-election as it exceeds judicial mandate.

name: KANE, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the initiative petition is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative authority and has a faulty gist, and should be struck down based on precedent.

name: ROWE, V.C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court should have followed precedent to strike the petition for constitutional infirmities (non-delegation, misleading gist) or explicitly overruled its precedent.

name: MUSSEMAN, JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that Oklahoma district courts' subject matter jurisdiction is not preempted in Indian Country and that the petitioner waived his claim by not raising it earlier.

name: ROWLAND, PRESIDING JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that criminal jurisdiction in Indian Country does not implicate the State of Oklahoma's subject matter jurisdiction, which is established by the Oklahoma Constitution and cannot be taken away by Congress.

name: HUDSON, VICE PRESIDING JUDGE
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's approach is contrary to established Federal law, misinterprets Indian Country jurisdictional challenges, and fails to apply the Bracker balancing test as mandated by the Supreme Court.

name: LUMPKIN, JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the opinion correctly defines subject matter jurisdiction and clarifies how preemption applies, aligning with Supreme Court guidance in Castro-Huerta.

name: LEWIS, JUDGE
description: Dissented, argued that states have no jurisdiction over crimes committed by Indians in Indian Country unless expressly conferred by Congress, and the petitioner's challenge to jurisdiction was not waived.

name: Kane, C.J.
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part with no specific opinion provided.

name: Kuehn, J.
description: Concurred in Parts I and II but dissented in Part III, arguing that the Legislature's actions constituted impermissible micro-management of the Governor's delegated authority to negotiate compacts, violating the separation-of-powers doctrine.

name: COMBS, J.
description: Concurred, delivering the opinion that the trial court erred in denying a temporary injunction against the three Acts, which place unnecessary burdens on a woman's constitutional right to terminate a pregnancy to preserve her life.

name: Kauger
description: Concurred, arguing that any analysis of an abortion statute must consider the life of the mother.

name: Kane, C.J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's analysis fails to consider the rights of the unborn and that the court had already addressed the constitutionality of elective abortion.

name: Rowe, V.C.J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's claim of not ruling on elective abortion rights is misleading, as previous rulings upheld a statute criminalizing elective abortion.

name: Darby, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the district court did not abuse its discretion based on the law at the time and that the majority misapplied the standard of review.

name: Kuehn, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the Oklahoma Constitution does not support an abortion right, which should be decided by the people, and that the majority improperly found the bills unconstitutional without a proper record.

name: EDMONDSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the petition failed to state a claim that the Lengthy Trial Fund fee statute is an unconstitutional special law, finding the legislative determination regarding litigant classification to be reasonable.

name: DARBY
description: Concurred, argued that while he would dissent if the issue were new, stare decisis dictates the outcome based on previous rulings.

name: KANE, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the case presents different legal and factual issues than the previous case (OCRJ I) and stare decisis alone does not fully resolve it, and applying stare decisis could expand the reach of OCRJ I, which he believes was wrongly decided.

name: ROWE, V.C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that S.B. 1503 is distinguishable from the statute found unconstitutional in OCRJ I because S.B. 1503 places discretion with the physician to determine a medical emergency, which would have alleviated concerns in the prior case, and that the majority's characterization of S.B. 1503 as "even more extreme" is misplaced.

name: KUEHN, J.
description: Dissented, argued for the reasons given in his dissent in Oklahoma Call for Reproductive Justice v. Drummond.

name: GURICH, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Commission's interpretation is consistent with legislative intent and avoids constitutional due process issues by giving claimants the benefit of the longer limitations period.

name: KANE, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority disregarded clear statutory language by re-inserting "whichever is greater" into the statute, thereby substituting its own wisdom for legislative intent.

name: KAUGER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the right to preserve the life of the mother is deeply rooted in Oklahoma law and highlighted the incongruity of the challenged statute.

name: COMBS, J.
description: Concurred specially, argued that Article II, Section 2 of the Oklahoma Constitution provides a substantive right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, including personal autonomy and a right to privacy, which confers greater rights than the U.S. Constitution.

name: KANE, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority fashioned a right that does not exist in the Oklahoma Constitution, confusing what is provided with what is wished, and that the issue should be decided by the people.

name: ROWE, V.C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that abortion policy is a political question for the people to decide, not the court, and that the Oklahoma Constitution does not protect a right to abortion.

name: DARBY, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority created a new constitutional right based on a statutory exception, applied an incorrect standard of review, and was perplexed by the court's claim of not ruling on elective abortion while doing so.

name: KUEHN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court should exercise judicial restraint and not create a right where none explicitly exists in the Oklahoma Constitution, leaving policy decisions to the Legislature and the people.

name: KANE, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that Oklahoma law does not recognize a cause of action for a voluntarily intoxicated adult against a commercial vendor for self-inflicted injuries or against a bettor for injuries sustained while driving intoxicated.

name: ROWE, V.C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the facts are appalling, the court should not expand civil liability beyond common law or statutory mandates, as this responsibility rests with the Legislature.

name: Kauger, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's conclusion that the mother of the driver has no cause of action is contrary to the Oklahoma Constitution and statutes, which impose a broad duty to refrain from selling alcohol to intoxicated persons.

name: Gurich, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court's precedent in Ohio Casualty has no basis in law because the State Constitution and statutes impose a broad duty to refrain from selling alcohol to an intoxicated person, and the concept of 'voluntary consumption' should not negate the cause of action.

name: Darby, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the egregious facts of the case, where employees over-served and then bet an intoxicated person to drive, should allow for a cause of action, and the court's public policy reasoning for protecting innocent third parties but not the intoxicated driver is flawed.

name: Combs, J.
description: Other, was disqualified from the case.

name: KAUGER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Production Tax Credits are intangible personal property and thus exempt from ad valorem taxation under the Oklahoma Constitution, and all other justices concurred with this majority opinion.

name: KAUGER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the statutes were an unconstitutional delegation of legislative authority to the extent they required the Governor to declare an emergency for local school districts to make health decisions.

name: FISCHER, S.J.
description: Concurred in part with the majority regarding the unconstitutional delegation of legislative power in section 1210.190, but dissented from upholding section 1210.189, arguing it is an unconstitutional special law regulating public schools.

name: COMBS, J.
description: Concurred in part with the majority regarding the unconstitutional delegation of legislative power in section 1210.190, but dissented from upholding section 1210.189, arguing it is an unconstitutional special law regulating public schools.

name: ROWE, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court committed reversible error by admitting prejudicial evidence of pending criminal charges and including them in jury instructions, violating the parents' right to a fair trial.

name: Darby, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court abused its discretion by admitting evidence of pending criminal charges, which deprived parents of constitutional due process and a fair trial regarding their right to raise their children.

name: Combs, J.
description: Dissented, argued that any error in admitting evidence of pending criminal charges was harmless given the overwhelming evidence of heinous and shocking abuse, and the majority applied the wrong standard of harmless error review.
